c.tagline: Bold modern architecture and Europe's biggest port.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; official taxis carry a blue licence plate. Booking apps are common.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU emergency number for police, ambulance and fire in the Netherlands.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: No real no-go zones; a few pockets of Rotterdam-Zuid feel edgy late at night but hold nothing for tourists.
Pickpockets work Centraal station, busy trams and markets; lock your bike well, as bike theft is rife.

hood_desc: The rebuilt modern heart of the city around the Markthal, Cube Houses, Lijnbaan shopping street and Rotterdam Centraal; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers.

A futuristic waterfront quarter on the south bank at the foot of the Erasmus Bridge, home to landmark towers, Hotel New York and cruise terminals; suits travelers who want skyline views and design hotels.
A former docklands peninsula turned foodie hotspot, with the Fenix Food Factory, theatres and buzzing restaurants; good for those chasing dining and a lively, local scene.
A rare surviving historic harbor of 17th-century canals, the Pilgrim Fathers' church and craft breweries; a calmer, characterful area a short metro ride west of the centre.
The arts-and-nightlife strip around Witte de Withstraat and the Museumpark galleries, packed with bars, cafes and street art; best for creative, going-out travelers.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe everywhere in the Netherlands.

transit.hours: Metro and trams run roughly 6am-midnight; BOB night buses cover the city into the small hours on Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless debit/credit card or phone directly on metro gates, trams and buses via OVpay — no card purchase needed — or buy a rechargeable OV-chipkaart. Fares are distance-based (roughly €1-4 / US$1-4.30 per trip); a RET 2-hour ticket from the driver is about €4.50 (~US$4.90).

places.name: Blaak Markt

places.name: Eateries on West-Kruiskade

places.name: Blaak Markt roti stands

food.name: Rotterdam craft beer
food.desc: A strong local brewing scene: hoppy IPAs and dark bocks from harbour breweries, usually poured with a two-finger head.

places.name: Kaapse Brouwers

places.name: Stadsbrouwerij De Pelgrim

places.name: Locus Publicus

landmarks: Erasmusbrug (Erasmus Bridge)
The elegant 139-metre swan-necked bridge spanning the Nieuwe Maas, Rotterdam's defining silhouette linking the city centre to the Wilhelminapier skyline.
Markthal
A horseshoe-shaped market hall with apartments arching over food stalls beneath the Netherlands' largest artwork, an 11,000-square-metre cornucopia of giant produce.
Kubuswoningen (Cube Houses)
Piet Blom's gravity-defying tilted yellow cubes of 1984, an icon of Dutch structuralism where one show home reveals life inside a 45-degree world.
Euromast
A 185-metre tower from 1960 offering the Netherlands' highest public viewpoint, with a rotating glass lift, brasserie and abseiling for the daring.
Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen
A mirrored bowl-shaped art depot, the world's first fully accessible museum storage facility, stacking 155,000 artworks beside a rooftop forest with skyline views.
Grote of Sint-Laurenskerk
Rotterdam's only surviving medieval building, a late-Gothic church that outlasted the 1940 bombing and anchors the reborn city around the Erasmus statue.
Historic Delfshaven
A miraculously preserved old harbour of gabled houses and the Pilgrim Fathers Church, from whose quay the Pilgrims departed for America in 1620.
Hotel New York and Wilhelminapier
The ornate former Holland America Line headquarters, launch point for a million emigrants, now a beloved cafe amid the pier's dramatic modern towers.
SS Rotterdam
The lovingly restored 1959 flagship of the Holland America Line, permanently moored in Katendrecht as a floating hotel, museum and time capsule of ocean-liner glamour.
Fenix
A 1923 harbor warehouse in Katendrecht reborn as a migration museum, its swirling steel Tornado staircase spiraling up to a rooftop panorama of the port.

ferry.note: Car and foot-passenger ferries to England leave from the Hoek van Holland terminal, part of Rotterdam and reachable on Metro line B.
